doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playing the acoustic harpsichord on record
summary: He recalls recording harpsichord on 'Uptown', the overdubbing needed, and how the idea came about.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah it’s great. This is also the record you did the harpsichord on.
[scats] — no, I’m singing “Take Five.” There was a —

The hardest thing about that was, you know the harpsichord, it wasn’t an electric harpsichord, it was an acoustic harpsichord. They’re so delicate, and so light, that, like if you notice in an orchestra even, when a harpsichord plays, the rest of the orchestra isn’t playing behind them. Like they’re playing passages, solo passages. Because the instrument is so light and so soft. And you can’t hammer it to play it.
It doesn’t make any difference, right.

Yeah you’ve got to play it lightly, yeah. So the way we had to do that, I had to record it with the rhythm section, you know on three different tracks, and then they take the rhythm section tracks and put them through the earphones and then I’d play it on the harpsichord and the harpsichord’s been boosted to the level in the earphones. But they
tell me that for release they had to boost it about five times to make it sound level. And that’s what it sounds like.
Where did the idea come from to use the harpsichord?

Actually there was a harpsichord in the studio. Somebody must have recorded some harpsichord music maybe before that and I was just fooling around with it, and the producer said, “Hey, let’s do a tune with you playing harpsichord.” I said, “Yeah, why not?” And we did. It’s been done before, I’m not the first one to do that. Johnny Guarnieri did it when he was with — I think it was Johnny Guarnieri, with the Gramercy Five Artie Shaw band. Yeah, they did a bunch of things with a harpsichord and a five piece combo. And probably they did it the same way because I don’t think they had the electric harpsichord then. Now they’ve got electric harpsichords, you know that they use for jazz or other pop music. And they can boost it up, and you can record right there on the same level.
